anf_compare.notes: Translated from the PG 74 Greek; no published English version was used for wording.

bible_refs.note: πρόβατα οἴκου Ἰσραήλ completes Οὐκ ἀπεστάλην εἰ μὴ εἰς τὰ ἀπολωλότα from the end of u11-rem-mid.
διάκονον ... περιτομῆς ... εἰς τὸ βεβαιῶσαι τὰς ἐπαγγελίας τῶν πατέρων; Cyril reads ἐκ περιτομῆς.
τὰ δὲ ἔθνη ὑπὲρ ἐλέους δοξάσαι τὸν θεόν; Cyril's εἰς ἔλαιον τοῖς ἐξ ἐθνῶν ... ἵνα καὶ αὐτοὶ δοξάσειαν paraphrases the verse.
The chain of prophecies Paul sets out (Psalm 18:49; Deuteronomy 32:43; Psalm 117:1; Isaiah 11:10), to which Cyril's closing sentence points.

choices.why: εἰς ἔλαιον: the copy-text reads ἔλαιον ('oil'); taken as ἔλεον ('mercy'), the sense of Romans 15:9 (ὑπὲρ ἐλέους) which Cyril is paraphrasing. Rendered 'for mercy'.

choices.english: Maker and Craftsman of all things
choices.why: γενεσιουργὸν καὶ τεχνίτην: 'author of coming-to-be and craftsman'; rendered 'Maker and Craftsman of all things' (τῶν ὅλων).
ἔδει γὰρ ἔδει: the doubled verb is Cyril's emphasis, kept as 'it was needful, truly needful'.
ἡ ὑπ' οὐρανόν: the feminine article implies γῆ or οἰκουμένη ('the land/world under heaven'); rendered 'the whole world under heaven'.
κατοικτείροντος Θεοῦ: genitive absolute, rendered 'because God had compassion'.
ἁγίων ... ἐν πνεύματι: the holy prophets foreknew by the Holy Spirit; 'Spirit' is capitalized.

pass_a_gloss: [end of quotation begun in u11-rem-mid: I was not sent except to the lost] sheep (πρόβατα) of the house of Israel. therefore Paul will not speak falsely saying he became servant from circumcision to confirm (βεβαιῶσαι) the promises of the fathers, and to have been placed besides this by the God and Father also for oil/mercy to those from the nations (ἔθνη), that they also might glorify (δοξάσειαν) as maker of origins and craftsman of the whole the Saviour and Redeemer. for it was necessary, it was necessary, through much disobedience the circumcision insulting him unholily and not admitting the redemption from him, that the unspeakable (ἄφραστον) grace of God not seem to be ineffective, few and scarcely altogether of the believers from Israel having been saved; for this reason the calm from above being widened as it were upon all, the nations were received, and the mystery (μυστήριον) of the wisdom in Christ is seen not having missed the aim looking toward gentleness; for in place of those who slipped the [land] under heaven has been saved, God having compassion. and that the mystery had been proclaimed beforehand through the voice of saints who foreknew in the Spirit the things to be, he establishes by a most vivid setting-beside of the prophecies.
pass_b_english: …sheep of the house of Israel” (Matthew 15:24). So Paul does not speak falsely when he says that Christ became a servant from the circumcision to confirm the promises made to the fathers (Romans 15:8), and that besides this He was appointed by God the Father for mercy also to those from the nations, so that they too might glorify the Saviour and Redeemer as the Maker and Craftsman of all things (Romans 15:9).

For it was needful, truly needful, since the circumcision in its great disobedience insulted Him wickedly and would not accept the redemption He gave, that the unspeakable grace of God should not seem to have achieved nothing, when those from Israel who had believed and been saved were few, a bare handful. For this reason, as the calm that comes from above was spread wide, as it were, over all, the nations were received. And the mystery of the wisdom that is in Christ is seen not to have missed its aim, an aim set on kindness. For in place of those who had slipped, the whole world under heaven has been saved, because God had compassion.
And that the mystery had been proclaimed beforehand by the voice of holy men who foreknew in the Spirit what was to come, he establishes by setting out the prophecies most plainly (Romans 15:9–12).

review_notes: Staged translation is faithful. Two small fixes made in tr9.json: 'only a few … who believed, and those scarcely at all, had been saved' contradicted itself; ὀλίγων καὶ μόλις κομιδῆ marks how few were saved, now 'were few, a bare handful'. 'its aim, which looks toward gentleness' smoothed to 'an aim set on kindness' (ἡμερότης).
Opens mid-quotation: εἰ μὴ εἰς τὰ ἀπολωλότα ends u11-rem-mid; this section supplies πρόβατα οἴκου Ἰσραήλ. The leading ellipsis marks the join.
Page numbers 31 and 32 in the copy-text are dropped from the reading text.
εἰς ἔλαιον: the copy-text reads ἔλαιον ('oil'); taken as ἔλεον ('mercy'), the sense of Romans 15:9 (ὑπὲρ ἐλέους) which Cyril is paraphrasing. Rendered 'for mercy'.
διάκονον αὐτὸν γεγενῆσθαι: the subject αὐτόν is Christ, named in English.
γενεσιουργὸν καὶ τεχνίτην: 'author of coming-to-be and craftsman'; rendered 'Maker and Craftsman of all things' (τῶν ὅλων).
ἔδει γὰρ ἔδει: the doubled verb is Cyril's emphasis, kept as 'it was needful, truly needful'.
ἡ ὑπ' οὐρανόν: the feminine article implies γῆ or οἰκουμένη ('the land/world under heaven'); rendered 'the whole world under heaven'.
κατοικτείροντος Θεοῦ: genitive absolute, rendered 'because God had compassion'.
ἁγίων ... ἐν πνεύματι: the holy prophets foreknew by the Holy Spirit; 'Spirit' is capitalized.
The fragment ends with Cyril's reference to the prophecies of Romans 15:9–12; they are not quoted here.
